test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The average of 19 consecutive natural numbers is A. What is the sum of the largest and the smallest numbers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any sequence of consecutive natural numbers (Arithmetic Progression), the average is always the middle value.

The average is also equal to the mean of the first and last terms.

Formula: Average = (Smallest number + Largest number) ÷ 2

Given: Average = A

Sum of smallest and largest = 2 × Average = 2 × A = 2A

**∴ The correct answer is 2A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total consecutive terms (n) = 19, Average = A

Formula: Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ab962451a70a7cb89d6564dae8ebe79fdc795a94db3c9a8434555f6c4cbc908.png] 

⇒ Let the 19 consecutive natural numbers be x, (x + 1), (x + 2), ..., (x + 18).

⇒ Average = [Sum of all terms] ÷ 19

⇒ In an AP, Average = (Smallest + Largest) ÷ 2

⇒ A = [x + (x + 18)] ÷ 2

⇒ A = (2x + 18) ÷ 2

⇒ 2A = 2x + 18

⇒ Sum of smallest and largest = x + (x + 18) = 2x + 18

⇒ From the previous step, 2x + 18 = 2A

**∴ The correct answer is 2A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of AP

For any sequence in Arithmetic Progression, the Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2 = Middle Term (if n is odd).

Sum of n Consecutive Numbers

The sum of n consecutive natural numbers starting from x is S = (n ÷ 2) × [2x + (n − 1)].

Middle Term Location

If the number of terms n is odd, the middle term is the [(n + 1) ÷ 2]th term, which represents the average.
